text:
For 40 minutes, Calgary had the only goal that mattered, a Matt Coronato power-play wrister in the first period that carried a 6 percent chance of going in. Then Vancouver played a third period that made the scoreboard look backward. The Canucks out-chanced the Flames 2.14 to 0.50 in expected goals over the final 20 minutes and scored four times.

Liam Ohgren tied it 1:28 into the third on a wrister, and Elias Pettersson (the defenseman) put Vancouver ahead at 9:04 with a backhand off Ohgren's pass. Drew O'Connor made it 3-1 at 16:33. Just 43 seconds later, Aatu Räty finished a 79 percent chance for the fourth. Räty played only 9:30 but took three shots on goal, and his own expected goals of 0.88 led the team.

The full-game numbers say Vancouver earned this. The Canucks led 3.61 to 1.70 in total expected goals and would win 71 percent of simulated replays. Shot attempts were even at 63 each, so the difference was quality. Linus Karlsson and Tom Willander drove it from the back and middle of the lineup, with Karlsson's on-ice expected goals at 2.07 for and 0.63 against. Leevi Meriläinen stopped 23 of 24 against 1.70 expected, while Devin Cooley allowed three against 2.82. Vancouver went 0 for 5 on the power play and still won comfortably.
